readout: Complementation fitness of a yeast cys4-delta strain at low vitamin B6; higher is more functional
assay_method: Functional complementation of a Saccharomyces cerevisiae cys4-delta strain by human CBS, which restores growth without glutathione supplementation. A variant library made by POPCode mutagenesis was assayed in parallel and scored by the authors' TileSeq framework, at low and high vitamin B6 to read out B6 remediability. Per-variant scores were taken from the authors' MaveDB deposit, using the raw score sets rather than the imputed and refined ones.
remark: Of the deposit's 11478 rows, 411 nonsense rows are dropped, a premature stop not being writable as a substitution, and 0 further rows carry no score, and 3333 rows collapse into 2355 duplicate groups whose members are the same protein variant reached by different codons and whose spread is exactly zero in every group. The 517 synonymous rows are the wild-type protein and collapse to the single WT row at their mean, whose worst spread is 1.520. The raw score set is used; the deposit's imputed-and-refined sets for the same condition are not curated, imputed values being computed rather than measured. The article is open access but neither Europe PMC's fullTextPDF route nor the publisher's counter/pdf link returns a PDF to an automated request, so it is not redistributed in papers/.
